headline: Whale Watching Tours and Saguenay Fjord Access
reservation: While the village itself is open access, whale watching excursions and Parc national du Fjord-du-Saguenay camping require separate bookings. During the peak summer migration, boat tours and shoreline accommodations fill rapidly; confirm all commercial services through official regional operators.

days.title: Marine Mammals and Fjord Vistas

stops.name: Pointe-de-l'Islet
stops.detail: Walk the wooden boardwalks to spot whales from the shore where the Saguenay meets the St. Lawrence.

stops.name: CIMM (Marine Mammal Interpretation Centre)
stops.detail: Learn about the resident beluga population and the unique ecology of the marine park.

days.driving: Local walking within the village; vehicle transfer only for distant trailheads.
days.note: Marine temperatures are significantly cooler than in town; dress in layers for the shoreline.

days.title: Coastal Dunes and Coastal Trails
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from the Village Center

stops.name: Dunes de Tadoussac
stops.detail: Explore the massive sand terraces formed by glacial retreat and watch for migratory birds.

stops.name: Sentier du Fjord
stops.detail: Hike the initial section of this long-distance trail for elevated views over the Saguenay Fjord.

days.driving: Allow 15 minutes to reach the dunes; conditions vary by weather.
days.note: The dunes area can be extremely windy; eye protection is suggested for sandy conditions.

days.title: Saguenay Shoreline Discovery

stops.name: Tadoussac-Baie-Sainte-Catherine Ferry
stops.detail: Cross the mouth of the Saguenay Fjord on the year-round ferry for panoramic views of the cliffs.

stops.name: Baie-de-Tadoussac
stops.detail: Stroll the historic bay front to see the iconic red-roofed hotel and historic chapel.

days.driving: Ferry transit takes approximately 10-20 minutes; allow for wait times during peak periods.
days.note: Ferry service is free and runs 24 hours, but peak summer traffic can cause significant delays.

intel.title: Village Congestion
intel.text: Parking near the marina is limited and often metered during the summer season. Utilize the peripheral public lots near the dunes to avoid pedestrian congestion in the historic core.

intel.title: Coastal Coverage
intel.text: Cellular service is reliable within Tadoussac village but drops off quickly when hiking deeper into the Fjord-du-Saguenay trails. Carry physical maps for inland explorations.

intel.title: Regional Stations
intel.text: Fuel is available in Tadoussac, but prices may be higher than in Saguenay or Quebec City. Ensure a full tank if planning to drive the remote Highway 138 northeast.

intel.title: Whale Migration
intel.text: Peak whale activity typically occurs from July through September. Sightings from shore are possible but vary based on tide levels and food source movement.

intel.title: Park Entry Fees
intel.text: While the village is free, entry to the Parc national du Fjord-du-Saguenay sectors requires a daily access pass. These can be purchased online via the SEPAQ website to save time.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at Saguenay-Bagotville (YBG), drive Highway 172 to the Fjord or Highway 138 from Quebec City.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are perfect for this region; note that RVs must use specific lanes on the Tadoussac ferry.
plan.goldenHour: Sentier de la Pointe-de-l'Islet offers stunning views of the fjord against the setting sun in late summer.
